questions.q: What does the -v mysql-data:/var/lib/mysql flag in a docker run command accomplish?
options: It creates a named volume that persists the database data across container removal and recreation
It sets the root password for the container
It exposes the MySQL port to the host
It has no effect on data persistence
questions.explain: Without a volume, data lives only inside the container's writable layer and is lost when the container is removed.

questions.q: Which command starts and enables the MySQL service on a systemd-based Linux install?
options: sudo systemctl enable --now mysql
sudo mysql_secure_installation
docker run mysql:8.0
SELECT VERSION();
questions.explain: systemctl enable --now both starts the service immediately and configures it to start on boot.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT part of what mysql_secure_installation does, per this lesson?
options: Installing the InnoDB storage engine
Removing anonymous user accounts
Disabling remote root login
Removing the test database
questions.explain: InnoDB ships with MySQL by default; mysql_secure_installation handles post-install hardening, not engine installation.

questions.q: Why does mysql_secure_installation disable remote root login?
options: To close a well-known attack surface by restricting root to connecting only from localhost
Because root accounts are being removed entirely
Because remote connections are disabled for all users
It's a cosmetic setting with no security purpose
questions.explain: Restricting root to localhost significantly reduces the attack surface of a fresh MySQL install.

questions.q: What does running `mysql -u root -p -e "SELECT VERSION();"` confirm after an install?
options: That the server accepted the connection, credentials are correct, and the client can reach the port
That mysql_secure_installation has been run
That the InnoDB storage engine is the default
That remote root login is disabled
questions.explain: A successful version query is the basic 'can I even get in' connectivity check after any fresh install.
